statement: SK Hynix has committed $38.3 billion of investment through 2031, including a $4 billion HBM packaging plant in Indiana targeting 2029 production, while its CEO says the memory shortage could persist through 2030.
why: Memory capex of this size adds real HBM supply, but only late in the decade, so the near-term gap between HBM demand and available bits stays open.

impact.mechanism: Large multi-year memory and advanced-packaging capex eventually loosens the HBM bottleneck that caps accelerator output, but the stated shortage horizon through 2030 means the relief lands beyond the current planning window.
